 Manufactured homes offer an affordable alternative in an expensive housing market. 
 Published Mon, Oct 19 2026 Kelsey Neubauer Reporter, CNBC Select Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Manufactured homes provide an affordable alternative in an expensive housing market : In May, the average sales cost was $130,500, compared to $582,300 for an existing home, according to the National Association of Realtors. 
 Prefabricated homes are housing units made in a factory and shipped to a location — they can be as elaborate as a multimillion-dollar abode in a ritzy ZIP code and as humble as a studio mobile home. 
 There are 6.6 million occupied mobile or manufactured homes throughout the U.S., according to 2024 estimates from the American Community Survey, the most recent data available. While these homes made up 5.1% of homes built in 2025, industry experts predict demand will grow 6.5% through 2030, according to the Modular Building Institute. 
 Popularity is rising amid a spike in housing affordability — home prices are near a record high, and mortgage rates are above 7.0% . 
 Financing a prefab home depends on the structure type, where it's built, and whether it's permanent. CNBC Select reviewed lenders to find the best based on loan options and the types of homes they finance. 
 To learn more about how we made our selections, check out our methodology .

 Best for long construction period: Citizens Bank
 Who's this for? Citizens Bank is a great option if you think you may have an extended building phase. It's one of Select's favorite lenders for construction loans because of its longer-than-average 18-month loan term. 
 Standout benefits : Qualifying bank customers can get a 0.125% interest rate discount on their mortgage if they set up autopay.

 Borrowers can earn up to $9,500 by buying their home through HomeStory, making it a great option for those who need extra cash to replenish their savings after they sign their deed.

 Best for modular homes: Guild Mortgage
 Who's this for? Unlike many big-name mortgage lenders, Guild Mortgage offers mortgages specifically to construct modular homes. It was awarded the United States Department of Agriculture's USDA Manufactured Housing Champion in 2026, due to its loan origination volume, modular-specific underwriting and effort to help rebuild Paradise, California after the 2018 wildfire with its CrossMod Manufactured homes — a design with elements of both prefab and site-built homes. 
 Standout benefits : Guild Mortgage also offers a wide range of other specialty mortgages and down payment assistance programs for first-time homebuyers that can be used by those purchasing a prefab or site-built home alike.

 Who's this for? Triad is one of the biggest names in chattel mortgages — or a home loan used on a movable abode, where the owner doesn't necessarily own the land underneath. This is a type of loan you may use if you plan to purchase a mobile home. 
 Standout benefits: Triad offers a variety of tools, including a loan and affordability calculator on its easy-to-use website.

 Learn More View More Best for prefab accessory dwelling units: TD Bank
 Who's this for? If you're looking to add a unit to your property, TD Bank is a great option. One of the most common ways to finance this kind of project is to borrow against your home's value with a home equity loan or home equity line of credit, also known as a HELOC. TD offers both with flexible, favorable terms: you can borrow as little as $10,000 with a home equity loan, which is less than most lenders, and as much as $6 million, which is more than most lenders. Plus, it also offers personal loans if you prefer to finance your ADU that way. 
 Standout benefits:  With TD Bank, you can convert your eligible variable-rate HELOC valued at $5,000 or more into a fixed-rate option. TD also offers a 0.25% discount for eligible checking account customers.

 What is a prefabricated house? 
 A prefabricated house is constructed off-site — either partially or fully — in a factory. 
 Modular construction
 The most common type of prefab housing construction is modular. Once sections — or modules — are fully built, they're loaded onto trucks and driven to the site. Once there, they're assembled into one unit and remain on the property as the primary residence, as any other single-family unit would. 
 Panels
 Panelized construction is when certain elements of a house — like walls and floors — are built in a factory and delivered. Unlike modular homes, which are large sections of the home joined on site, panelized homes must be assembled piecemeal on site. 
 Mobile homes
 This type of prefabricated housing is built to be transportable, and the unit's owner doesn't always own the land it sits on.
 Accessory dwelling units 
 Many accessory dwelling units — or backyard tiny homes — are prefabricated and brought to their final location. Unlike other homes, ADUs are secondary structures on the same property. Not all jurisdictions allow these structures, but several states — most notably California — have rolled back restrictions to create more housing and make the market more affordable. 
 Financing options for prefabricated houses
 The right financing option depends on the type of prefabricated home. Below is a table of the financing options you can use, based on what you're building. 
 Types of prefabricated homes and financing options
 House type What is it How to finance 
 Modular houses Houses that are built in a factory in modules and then transported to a permanent location Short-term construction loans, construction-to-permanent loans 
 Accessory dwelling units Secondary structures on existing properties HELOC, home equity loan, personal loan, cash-out refinance, renovation loans 
 Panelized homes Houses that feature wall and floor panels that were made in a factory and delivered. Short-term construction loans, construction-to-permanent loans 
 Manufactured houses Houses constructed in full at a factory and dropped onto the property at a permanent site owned by the people who own the structure Short-term construction loans, construction-to-permanent loans 
 Mobile homes Houses built in a factory, designed to sit atop a rented plot in a mobile home park. The owners of the unit do not necessarily own the land underneath. Chattel mortgages

 Our methodology
 CNBC Select analyzed dozens of prefab mortgages offered by banks, credit unions, online lenders and others. We focused on the following features:
 Loan types : We included lenders who have products specifically for prefabricated homes, including construction loans, chattel mortgages, home equity products and loans to refinance a temporary mortgage used during the construction process. 
 Credit score : Most lenders require a FICO score of 620 or higher to qualify for a mortgage. 
 Closing times: We weighted lenders more heavily for shorter-than-average closing times or those that guaranteed on-time closing.
 Fees: Mortgages include a variety of charges, including origination, application and underwriting fees, appraisals, title insurance, attorneys and other closing costs. When possible, we noted if a lender had lower fees, discounts or waived certain fees.
 Application process: We considered whether lenders offered an online preapproval and application process and whether they had physical branches for an in-person experience. 
 Customer service: We weighted lenders more heavily for high scores on J.D. Power's mortgage origination and servicing surveys. We noted whether they had robust customer service phone hours, a website with an online chat feature, and educational resources.
 We also considered CNBC Select audience data, when available, including general demographics and engagement with our content and tools.
 Based on those criteria, our picks for the best mortgage lenders for prefab homes are:
 Best for permanent prefab homes:  Citizens Bank 
 Best for modular homes:  Guild Mortgage 
 Best for mobile homes: Triad Financial Services 
 Best for prefab accessory dwelling units:  TD Bank 
 Best for post-construction permanent loan:  Rocket Mortgage
